renderer_investigation.question: What is the smallest production path for native PS4 drawing of G3dSnapshot data while preserving the current CPU fallback and DS composition semantics?
scope: engine/platform/plat_gl3d.c and engine/platform/plat_sdlgpu3d.c feature and fallback behavior
demo/eidos_boot.c PS4 and generic GPU frame paths
engine/platform/ps4/video_ps4.cpp GNMX resources and command submission
evidence: G3dSnapshot owns transformed clip-space vertices, indices, polygons, decoded texture copies, and DS render state.
GL and SDL GPU backends consume G3dSnapshot and report supported frame features through g3d_hw_gpu_features; unsupported frames retain CPU rasterization.
The PS4 boot path does not create EidosPlatform: boot_render_ps4 calls g2d_hw_render_dsmem and draws the resulting 256x192 DS images through a final GNMX compatibility pass.

The official SDK sample archive includes GNMX vertex-buffer, vertex-shader, depth-target, indexed-draw, and submit examples; the current PS4 backend only binds pixel shaders for fullscreen compatibility passes.
renderer_investigation.decision: Keep the PS4 frame path and CPU rasterizer intact while prototyping a dedicated GNMX snapshot adapter. Do not advertise snapshot features as GPU-supported or enable raster skipping until feature coverage and fallback boundaries are proven.
renderer_investigation.implemented_slice: Added checked triangle/quad-fan conversion from G3dSnapshot clip-space fixed-point vertices and RGB bytes into a linear float vertex stream in engine/platform/ps4/snapshot_vertices_ps4.c. The helper rejects malformed indices/counts and insufficient capacity before writing. It is compiled into the PS4 platform target and covered by a host CTest regression. Added two official PSSL shader sources for the converted flat-color vertex format, registered offline compilation and embedding, and added shader-blob accessors. They are prototypes and are not yet bound to GNMX. Added GNMX vertex shader parsing/relocation, fetch shader and input-offset setup, interleaved vertex-buffer binding, and a flat triangle-list scanout draw. The standalone minimal diagnostic now exercises it; the game path remains unchanged.
renderer_investigation.validation: Strict host C99 test passes; CMake configured the full 427-unit boot and 976-source overlay graph and built test_ps4_snapshot_vertices (1/1 passed); official Orbis clang compiled the new helper with -Wall -Wextra -Werror. Official PSSL compiler generated 404-byte VS and 312-byte PS; an isolated seven-program manifest verified source/binary hashes and sizes; Orbis C++ compiled shader_blobs_ps4.cpp with generated headers. Official CMake built eidos_platform_ps4 and linked eidos_ps4_minimal.elf with all seven PSSL programs. ELF SHA-256 ab2199325c28b3d77532d9daf25ab9218aa6b440d2b7e39a33bba80aad4a45d7. Seven manifest source/binary hashes and sizes match. No hardware capture.
missing_evidence: Physical-console execution and image capture of the diagnostic triangle.
Game boot path connection to actual G3dSnapshot frames.
Texture/material/depth/blend semantics, explicit capability classifier, and CPU fallback behavior for partially supported frames.
renderer_investigation.next_experiment: After a physical capture confirms the diagnostic pipeline, connect a bounded set of real snapshot primitives behind an explicit diagnostic switch, and compare their raster output against the CPU renderer before enabling any GPU feature flags.
renderer_investigation.effort_budget: One bounded implementation checkpoint; stop after the isolated target build and conversion evidence, or record the exact SDK/API blocker and next discriminating check.
renderer_investigation.stopping_condition: Do not enable g3d_hw_skip_raster or claim production renderer coverage without physical image evidence, semantic differential checks, feature classification, and a whole-frame fallback for unsupported content.
